title: The Todo tutorial repository keeps one branch per step with a matching complete branch, so a learner can start anywhere or diff against a checkpoint
content:
The Todo List is the worked example used throughout the Build track, and the reference implementation at **`powerhouse-inc/todo-tutorial`** is organised so a learner never has to start from scratch:

- each step has a **starting branch** (`step-1-…`) and a **completed branch** (`step-1-complete-…`);
- the `step-1-` branch **matches what `ph init todo-tutorial` produces**, so a local project and the repository begin identical;
- comparing work against a checkpoint is `git diff your-branch step-1-complete-…`, or "compare with branch" in the GitHub UI.

One setup detail is easy to get wrong and expensive: when forking, **uncheck "copy the main branch only"** — otherwise every step branch is lost and the diff workflow the tutorial is built on stops working. Then clone the fork and `pnpm install`.

What the finished package demonstrates, which doubles as a map of the Build track: a `TodoList` document model with state schema and operations; reducer operation handlers **and their unit tests**; a document editor wired to the model's operations; a custom **Drive Explorer** for managing many Todo Lists in a drive; and a shared component displaying stats in **both** the editor and the Drive Explorer — the last one being the piece that shows a component crossing the editor/drive-app boundary.

The same example is taught twice on purpose: the Manual Todo tutorial builds a basic package by hand, and the Document Model Creation mastery track re-derives it with the theory plus advanced extensions (computed `stats`, the Drive Explorer, the shared component).
